chunks: of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then when they displeased Us, We inflicted retribution on them' [43:55] —

He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not grieve as we grieve. But He created friends (awliya') for Himself who grieve and are pleased, and they are created, nurtured beings. So He made their pleasure His own pleasure and their displeasure His own displeasure, because He made them the inviters to Him and the guides toward Him.
For this reason they became as such, yet it is not that it (grief) reaches Allah as it reaches His creatures. Rather, this is the meaning of what He said regarding that.

And He has said: 'Whoever insults a friend of Mine has declared war against Me and called Me to it.' And He said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah' [4:80]. And He said: 'Indeed, those who swear allegiance to you do but swear allegiance to Allah; the hand of Allah is above their hands' [48:10].

So all of this and the like of it is upon what I mentioned to you, and likewise is the pleasure and the anger and other things that are similar to that. Had it been that grief and weariness were to truly reach Allah — and He is the One who created them both — it would be permissible for one to say that one day the Creator would perish, because when anger and weariness enter Him, change would enter Him, and when change enters Him, annihilation cannot be ruled out.

Then the Originator would not be distinguished from the originated, nor the Powerful from the one over whom power is exercised, nor the Creator from the created. Exalted is Allah above this speech, an immense exaltation. Rather, He is the Creator of things not out of need. So when He created not out of need, limitation and modality are impossible regarding Him. So understand, if Allah the Exalted wills.'

key_terms.أولياء: Awliya', friends/allies of God; in Shia theology refers specifically to the Imams
key_terms.الأسف: Grief, sorrow, displeasure; the emotion attributed to God in Quran 43:55
key_terms.الحد والكيف: Limitation and modality; anthropomorphic categories inapplicable to God
key_terms.الدعاة والأدلاء: The inviters and guides; roles assigned to the Imams as God's representatives
key_terms.المكوِّن والمكوَّن: The Originator and the originated (Creator-creation distinction)
key_terms.لا لحاجة: Not out of need; God's creation is free from need, making change impossible in Him

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about divine grief and the awliya' in commentary on Quran 43:55?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expounding on Quran 43:55 ('Then when they displeased Us, We inflicted retribution'). The Imam explains that divine 'grief' or 'displeasure' attributed to God in scripture must be understood through the awliya' (divinely appointed friends/Imams): God created them such that their pleasure and anger reflect His own, because they are His appointed guides and inviters. The Imam then makes a rigorous theological argument — if such emotions were taken as literally applying to God, it would imply change and impermanence in the Divine, which is theologically impossible since God creates not out of need, making limitation and modality inapplicable to Him. This positions the Imams as the locus of divine will, grounding Shia walaya theology in Quranic interpretation and divine transcendence (tanzih).
